rulings.Case Title: ROSA MARTINEZ VS. AIRBNB, INC. ET AL
rulings.Calendar Matter: Defendants Airbnb, Inc. And Airbnb Payments, Inc.?S Second Notice Of Motion And Motion To File Confidential Documents Under Seal; Memorandum Of Points And Authorities In Support Thereof
rulings.Rulings: On the Law & Motion/Discovery calendar for August 27, 2026, line 1. DEFENDANTS AIRBNB, INC., AIRBNB PAYMENTS, LLC'S Motion To File Confidential Documents Under Seal. Defendants Airbnb, Inc. and Airbnb Payments, Inc.'s motion to seal documents specified in its notice of motion is granted. As to the categories of information specified in the moving papers, the court finds that Airbnb's nonpublic aggregate business data, internal deliberations and strategic planning, proprietary business information, and employee and user information are private information, as to which Airbnb's interest in maintaining confidentiality overcomes the public right of access to the court's records. For employee and user information, there is a privacy interest by employees and users. For proprietary business processes, Airbnb has protected trade secrets. For safety information, the court credits the Chauvet declaration that Airbnb's candid discussions about safety measures would be chilled without confidentiality protection. These overriding interests support sealing the record, the sealing is narrowly tailored, no less restrictive means exist to protect the interests, and there is a substantial probability that the overriding interests would be compromised if the record were not sealed. For the 9:00 a.m. calendar, all attorneys and parties may appear in Department 301 remotely or in person. Remote hearings will be conducted by videoconference using Zoom. (Dept. 301 Zoom ID 161 502 4290; Passcode 700956.) To appear remotely at the hearing, go to the court's website at sfsuperiorcourt.org under "Online Services," navigate to "Tentative Rulings," and click on the appropriate link, or dial the corresponding phone number. Any party who contests a tentative ruling must send an email to contestdept301tr@sftc.org with a copy to all other parties by 4pm stating, without argument, the portion(s) of the tentative ruling that the party contests. The subject line of the email shall include the line number, case name and case number. The text of the email shall include the name and contact information, including email address, of the attorney or party who will appear at the hearing. Counsel for the prevailing party is required to prepare a proposed order which repeats verbatim the substantive portion of the tentative ruling and must email it to contestdept301tr@sftc.org prior to the hearing even if the tentative ruling is not contested. The court no longer provides a court reporter in the Law & Motion or Discovery Department. Parties may retain their own reporter, who may appear in the courtroom or remotely. A retained reporter must be a California certified court reporter (CSR), for only a CSR's transcript may be used in California courts. If a CSR is being retained, include in your email all of the following: their name, CSR and telephone numbers, and their individual work email address. =(301/CVA)

Goel. Plaintiff Travis Fields's motion for reconsideration of the court's order granting summary judgment to the City and County of San Francisco is denied. To the extent Plaintiff relies upon Vehicle Code section 22655.5 as new authority, he does not state why this authority was not previously available to him. Plaintiff's motion largely relies on arguments and authorities that were already considered by the court. The requirements of Code of Civil Procedure, section 1008, are not met here, and the court declines to exercise its sua sponte discretion to reconsider its prior orders. rulings.Calendar Matter: Notice Of Motion And Motion To Compel Responses To Plaintiff'S Second Set Of Special Interrogatories
rulings.Rulings: On the Law & Motion/Discovery calendar for August 27, 2026, line 4. PLAINTIFF SWISH ANALYTICS, INC.'S Motion To Compel Responses To Plaintiff's Second Set Of Special Interrogatories. Swish Analytics Inc.'s motion to compel further responses to special interrogatories is denied as to interrogatory 7 and granted as to 8. No sanctions are awarded. Swish's meet and confer efforts were sufficient. With respect to 7, defendants Oddsjam Inc. and Opticodds Inc.'s (collectively Oddsjam) responses are sufficiently complete and responsive. Swish requested information about preservation of log data and the existence of log data as of December 20, 2024. Oddsjam responded that its software does not create logs. It further explained that it does not consider odds data to be logs, but described what it has done to preserve odds data since that date. Oddsjam's reading of the interrogatory is reasonable. With respect to 8, in response to a request for monthly revenues, Oddsjam produced incomplete documentation and relied on Code of Civil Procedure, section 2030.230. Swish shows that the referenced documents do not fully and completely respond to the interrogatory and that Oddsjam has the ability to answer the interrogatory at least partially and more fully as to revenue, including revenue from enterprise clients. (Kowalski Decl., Exs. 22-24.) In addition, Oddsjam does not respond to the portion of the interrogatory concerning attribution of revenue to other entities. Oddsjam shall amend by September 8, 2026. No sanctions are awarded; both parties' discovery position had substantial justification. For the 9:00 a.m. calendar, all attorneys and parties may appear in Department 301 remotely or in person. rulings.Rulings: On the Law & Motion/Discovery calendar for August 27, 2026, line 13. DEFENDANT JEFFREY FROST'S DEMURRER to Amended COMPLAINT. The demurrer is sustained without leave to amend for the reasons stated in the companion order on Sutter Valley Hospitals' demurrer. For the 9:00 a.m. calendar, all attorneys and parties may appear in Department 301 remotely or in person. Remote hearings will be conducted by videoconference using Zoom. (Dept. 301 Zoom ID 161 502 4290; Passcode 700956.) To appear remotely at the hearing, go to the court's website at sfsuperiorcourt.org under "Online Services," navigate to "Tentative Rulings," and click on the appropriate link, or dial the corresponding phone number. Any party who contests a tentative ruling must send an email to contestdept301tr@sftc.org with a copy to all other parties by 4pm stating, without argument, the portion(s) of the tentative ruling that the party contests. The subject line of the email shall include the line number, case name and case number. The text of the email shall include the name and contact information, including email address, of the attorney or party who will appear at the hearing. If no party contests the tentative ruling, it will be adopted verbatim in a minute order. The court no longer provides a court reporter in the Law & Motion or Discovery Department. Parties may retain their own reporter, who may appear in the courtroom or remotely. A retained reporter must be a California certified court reporter (CSR), for only a CSR's transcript may be used in California courts. If a CSR is being retained, include in your email all of the following: their name, CSR and telephone numbers, and their individual work email address. =(301/CVA)

rulings.Calendar Matter: Application For A Warrant For Seizing The Defendant'S Bank Account And Property Seizing Order
rulings.Rulings: On the Law & Motion/Discovery calendar for August 27, 2026, line 11. PLAINTIFF HAIQING QUI'S Application For A Warrant For Seizing The Defendant's Bank Account And Property Seizing Order. The unopposed application for a warrant to seize the defendant's bank account and property is denied. Plaintiff does not show proof that the moving papers were served on the defendant.
